text: A website for my cafe.

@Requester The brief is too thin to write a checkable charter. Four quick questions.
1. What is the cafe's name, and who is the site mainly for (for example nearby regulars, tourists, remote workers, families)?
2. What is the main thing a visitor should be able to do on the site?
   Option 1: See the menu and prices
   Option 2: Find location, opening hours and contact
   Option 3: Reserve a table
   Option 4: Order online for pickup or delivery
3. Which sections should the site include?
   Option 1: Menu
   Option 2: About / story
   Option 3: Photo gallery
   Option 4: Location with map and hours
4. Any hard rules on look, tone or content (for example brand colours, language, dietary labels, things to avoid)?
Paused: Identity is waiting on the Requester (J2.a: not enough information to work yet). Site v0 is in the preview. Answer Identity's question above to continue.

It's called Brew Lab, in Indiranagar. Show the menu with prices, opening hours 8am to 10pm every day, and our location. People should be able to pre-order coffee for pickup. Warm, modern, mobile-first.
@Adaptation Charter recorded for Brew Lab, Indiranagar, Bengaluru. The brief and answers were enough; menu items, prices, address and contact go in as marked placeholders.
@Adaptation Charter valid: statement present, 9 checkable done-when items. Work can start.

@Priority Two workflows close the gap. W1 builds the page shell: header, menu, hours and location with warm mobile-first styling, and marks every unknown as a placeholder. W2 adds the pre-order form with a running total. Together they cost 70 of the 100 budget, which leaves 30 for fixes.

proposal.name: Brew Lab page shell: header, menu, hours, location, styling
proposal.goal_gap: Site v0 has no Brew Lab content. Title, header, menu, hours and location sections are missing.
proposal.expected_outcome: A single HTML file with a viewport meta tag, a Brew Lab, Indiranagar, Bengaluru title and header, and mobile-first CSS with min-width media queries. It has a menu grouped by category with ₹ prices, hours of 8am to 10pm every day, and a location section with a map link. Menu items, prices and street address are visibly marked placeholders.
outputs: site/index.html (single file, no build step, no local dependencies)
proposal.completion_check: File has a viewport meta tag. Title and header contain 'Brew Lab' and 'Indiranagar, Bengaluru'. Menu has 2 or more categories, each item with a name and a ₹ price or a marked placeholder. Hours section reads 8am to 10pm for all 7 days. Location section has a map link or embed and a marked street-address placeholder. Base CSS targets small screens, larger layouts use min-width queries, and there is no horizontal scroll at 360px.

proposal.name: Pre-order form with running total
proposal.goal_gap: Visitors cannot pre-order coffee for pickup.
proposal.expected_outcome: A pre-order form in the same file. Visitors choose coffee items and quantities from the menu, enter a name and a pickup time, see a running ₹ total, and submit. The form states that it is a request for pickup and not a confirmed or paid order, because no real order channel exists yet. Placeholder prices are marked in the total.
outputs: site/index.html (updated with pre-order form and script)
proposal.completion_check: Form has item and quantity inputs, a name field, a pickup time field, a live total in ₹ and a submit button. Changing a quantity updates the total. Visible text says it is a pickup request, not a confirmed or paid order. There is no horizontal scroll at 360px, and the file is still a single file.

text: @Adaptation GRANT for both. W1 costs 45 and W2 costs 25 by the rate card, 70 in total, so 30 stays in reserve (three fixes at 8). W1 runs first only because W2 depends on it. Stop-loss: if a run hits its money limit before its completion check passes, it stops and you reshape it. I accept the trade-off that fixes beyond three would need a new request.
@Coordination Registered W-1 Brew Lab page shell: header, menu, hours, location, styling, W-2 Pre-order form with running total. Budget: 70/100 used.

@Priority W-1 runs first: it has no dependencies and W-2 needs its output. W-2 waits because both workflows write site/index.html, so W-1 must finish and pass its completion check before W-2 starts. Please check W-1's envelope (45 money, 2 calls, 20 min, 1 retry). Rule: Dependencies first, then one writer at a time on site/index.html, then lowest workflow id..
HOLD W-2: W-1 (W1-site-shell) must be done and pass its completion check, which also releases the lock on site/index.html

@Identity All 9 done-when items hold on the code and the mechanical check (360px and 1280px overflow 0, no JS errors, no broken links). Two low warnings only: Indiranagar sits in the hero rather than the header element, and the category names are unmarked. Audit finds the goal may be reached.

@Requester The goal is reached. The Brew Lab site is a single HTML file with the menu, 8am to 10pm hours for all 7 days, an Indiranagar location with a map link and embed, and a pre-order form with a running ₹ total. It works at 360px and 1280px with no horizontal scroll and no JS errors (Audit's mechanical check). The pre-order form says it is a pickup request, not a confirmed or paid order, because no real order channel exists yet. Two low warnings remain: Indiranagar is in the title and hero but not the header bar, and the category names (Hot Coffee, Cold Coffee, Bites) are ours, not yours. To make it live, send: real menu items and prices, street address and map pin, phone or contact, where pre-orders should go (WhatsApp, email or an ordering service) and whether payment is online, pickup rules, and any logo, photos or brand colours. Until then those stay as marked placeholders. Tell me if you want any changes.
